re_line: Trump-Xi summit's $30B tariff deal, Perdue's arms-offer disclosure, Senators press on Taiwan arms, Xi's National Day Taiwan line
editors_note: This is the first China Room Brief. It arrives every Friday with the week in US-China relations and what CSIS scholars have coming.

week_at_a_glance.headline: Beijing's fuel-export decision comes as Golden Week ends
week_at_a_glance.body: Chinese refiners suspended October fuel exports beyond Hong Kong and Macau, and PetroChina cancelled cargoes on Sep 30. Lianhe Zaobao reports it is unclear whether Beijing resumes export approvals when the holiday ends Oct 7. Reuters expects the suspension to tighten diesel and jet fuel across Asia.

week_at_a_glance.headline: No start date yet for the summit's tariff cuts
week_at_a_glance.body: USTR Jamieson Greer said no date is set for tariff cuts under the Board of Trade mechanism, and told Nikkei the US will unveil countermeasures against overproduction from China, Japan and others "within weeks." Reuters reported the US has slowed aircraft-part exports to China to build leverage.

week_at_a_glance.headline: Beijing's 1.2 trillion yuan liquidity injection lands Oct 8
week_at_a_glance.body: The PBOC's three-month reverse repo follows a nationwide mortgage-interest subsidy that took effect Oct 1. September manufacturing PMIs came in at 50.1, the first expansion after two months of contraction.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Twenty-one Democrats and four Republicans press for Taiwan arms
heard_on_the_hill.body: Twenty-one Democratic senators led by Jeanne Shaheen urged Trump to "immediately deliver congressionally approved defense assistance to Taiwan," citing $1.3 billion in appropriated funds and a $14 billion package approved nine months ago. Four Republican senators separately called for the assistance to be released.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Wicker: commitments to Taiwan must be upheld
heard_on_the_hill.body: Senate Armed Services Chair Roger Wicker made the point after meeting Alexander Yui, Taiwan's representative in Washington.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Johnson says the Taiwan arms delay is not trade leverage
heard_on_the_hill.body: Mike Johnson said Taiwan's stability matters to US security and the economy, dismissed suggestions that the delayed package is leverage in trade talks, and said Trump will have completed roughly $40 billion in Taiwan arms sales across his two terms.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Chinese car ban pushed past the midterms
heard_on_the_hill.body: The Senate put off a bill that would permanently bar Chinese-made cars until after the Nov 3 elections, AP reported; Reuters says senators plan a vote in November. Sen. Bernie Moreno said his separate bill, covering automakers with more than 15% Chinese ownership, would not touch Mercedes-Benz.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Bipartisan bill targets Chinese optical modules
heard_on_the_hill.body: A bipartisan group of senators proposed barring Chinese-made optical modules from federal national-security systems, with a five-year grace period. Shenzhen's ChiNext index fell 4.53% the next trading day.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Starbucks told to close its first Xinjiang stores
heard_on_the_hill.body: A US congressman demanded the closures, citing forced labor in the region, Reuters reported.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Lawmakers move to bar Chinese datacenter tech
heard_on_the_hill.body: Members of Congress are moving to keep Chinese-origin datacenter hardware and software out of sensitive US government systems, Reuters reported, after warnings about data-security risks to federal networks.

in_the_news.headline: China, US agree to AI-incident channel, $30bn tariff cuts in eight-point summit consensus
in_the_news.body: The two sides agreed to a channel for AI incidents and lower tariffs on $30 billion of goods each way, according to an eight-point readout Beijing published after Xi Jinping's Sep 23–25 state visit. The readout also lists a November AI dialogue and a pledge that Iran should not develop nuclear weapons, and the two militaries agreed to sign a crisis-communication memorandum.

in_the_news.headline: Trump asked Xi if China wanted to buy US weapons, ambassador says
in_the_news.body: Ambassador David Perdue told Fox News that Trump asked Xi at the summit whether China wanted to buy American weapons. The State Department said the US has no plans to sell weapons to China, and Trump told reporters he had "never heard of" the offer.

in_the_news.headline: Xi marks 77th PRC anniversary with hardened Taiwan message
in_the_news.body: Xi used his National Day address to sharpen Beijing's message on Taiwan, CNBC reported. At the Sep 30 reception he said China will "resolutely fight secessionist forces seeking 'Taiwanese independence,'" per Reuters; Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council said the phrasing is not new.

in_the_news.headline: US officials see Chinese invasion of Taiwan unlikely before 2028
in_the_news.body: Two current US officials, a former official and a fourth source told Reuters that Beijing is unlikely to use force against Taiwan before 2028, despite Xi's order that the PLA be ready by 2027. They point to the anti-corruption purge: two of seven Central Military Commission members, Xi among them, remain in active service.

in_the_news.headline: Beijing unveils mortgage subsidy, rate cut and 1.2 trillion yuan liquidity injection
in_the_news.body: The PBOC, the finance ministry and the financial regulator rolled out a nationwide mortgage-interest subsidy effective Oct 1, a cut to the Pledged Supplementary Lending rate and a 1.2 trillion yuan reverse repo set for Oct 8. September manufacturing PMIs returned to expansion at 50.1, CNBC reported.

research_roundup.headline: The Scope and Nature of the U.S.-China Competition
research_roundup.body: Michael J. Mazarr and colleagues open a multi-report RAND study: "The United States can protect its interests and gain leverage against China without blowing up the relationship."

research_roundup.headline: What did the Trump-Xi summit actually accomplish?
research_roundup.body: Brookings scholars including Ryan Hass, Yun Sun, Susan Thornton and Mireya Solís on "what the visit reveals about the future trajectory of U.S.-China relations."

research_roundup.headline: What Actually Happened at the Xi-Trump Summit
research_roundup.body: A ChinaFile conversation with Neil Thomas, Lizzi C. Lee, Lyle Morris and others: the summit "launched the U.S.-China bilateral dialogue on artificial intelligence" and left Taiwan and technology competition unresolved.

research_roundup.headline: Trump Had the Chance to Address U.S.-China AI Safety. He Threw Xi a Party Instead.
research_roundup.body: Jeffrey Prescott on the gap between "sobering risk and opulent inaction" on AI safety.

research_roundup.headline: A Trump-Xi Summit Scorecard
research_roundup.body: Bonnie Glaser grades the visit item by item, starting from Trump's bet that the trappings of respect would advance his agenda with Beijing.

research_roundup.headline: Why Trump Rolled Out the Red Carpet for Xi, and Why He Shouldn't Have
research_roundup.body: Dan Blumenthal and Ian Jones argue the treatment tells allies "that they are irrelevant as Beijing and Washington manage world affairs as coequal powers."
